name: Silvergate & Signature Banks

summary.text: Silvergate Bank (La Jolla, California) and Signature Bank (New York) were the two U.S. banks most used by cryptocurrency firms, including FTX, for dollar settlement. On March 8, 2023 Silvergate Capital Corporation announced it would wind down operations and voluntarily liquidate the bank with full repayment of deposits, days after discontinuing its Silvergate Exchange Network. On March 12, 2023 the New York State Department of Financial Services closed Signature Bank and the FDIC was named receiver, transferring deposits to a bridge bank under the systemic risk exception. The Federal Reserve's Office of Inspector General found in September 2023 that supervisors did not act quickly enough on Silvergate's crypto concentration, and in July 2024 the SEC charged Silvergate and two former executives with misleading investors about its anti-money-laundering monitoring of customers including FTX.

facts.claim: The FDIC records that on March 12, 2023 Signature Bank, New York, was closed by the New York State Department of Financial Services and the FDIC was named receiver. The FDIC transferred all deposits and substantially all assets to Signature Bridge Bank, N.A., which it operated while marketing the institution to bidders; regulators said all depositors would be made whole, an action taken under the systemic risk exception.
facts.quote: On March 12, 2023, Signature Bank, New York, NY, was closed by the New York State Department of Financial Services and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) was named Receiver.

facts.claim: Signature Bank had total assets of about $110.36 billion and total deposits of roughly $88.59 billion as of December 31, 2022, according to the New York Department of Financial Services; its closure came amid fallout from Silicon Valley Bank's failure two days earlier.

facts.claim: On March 8, 2023 Silvergate Capital Corporation announced its intent to wind down operations and voluntarily liquidate Silvergate Bank, stating that an orderly wind-down and voluntary liquidation was the best path forward and that the plan included full repayment of all deposits. On March 3, 2023 it had announced the discontinuation of the Silvergate Exchange Network (SEN).
facts.quote: an orderly wind down of Bank operations and a voluntary liquidation of the Bank is the best path forward

facts.claim: On September 27, 2023 the Federal Reserve Board's Office of Inspector General released the executive summary of its review of the supervision of Silvergate Bank, attributing the bank's self-liquidation to rapid growth in deposits concentrated in the cryptocurrency industry coupled with weaknesses in corporate governance and risk management, finding that supervisors did not act quickly enough, and concluding that Silvergate should have filed an application with the Fed when it pivoted to a crypto-focused business model.
facts.quote: rapid growth in deposits concentrated in the cryptocurrency industry, coupled with weaknesses in its corporate governance and risk management

facts.claim: On July 1, 2024 the SEC charged Silvergate Capital Corporation, former CEO Alan Lane and former chief risk officer Kathleen Fraher with misleading investors about the bank's anti-money-laundering controls and monitoring of crypto customers including FTX, alleging its automated monitoring system failed to monitor more than $1 trillion of transactions on its payments platform; it separately charged Silvergate and former CFO Antonio Martino over disclosures of expected securities losses after FTX's collapse. Lane and Fraher settled without admitting or denying, with five-year officer-and-director bars and penalties of $1 million and $250,000; Martino contested the charges.
facts.quote: failed to monitor more than $1 trillion of transactions by customers on the bank's payments platform

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): 'regional crypto banks (Silvergate, Signature) forced into FDIC closure' is partly supported: Signature was closed by NYDFS with the FDIC as receiver, but Silvergate announced a voluntary liquidation and was not placed in FDIC receivership. The wording should distinguish the two.
The existing ftx file records (from a bankruptcy pleading) that Silvergate maintained 45 accounts for FTX affiliates including the North Dimension account; that pleading was not re-opened here.
The outcome of the SEC's contested case against former CFO Antonio Martino, and any FDIC or NYDFS post-mortem on Signature's crypto deposits, were not researched.
The full Fed OIG report was not released publicly; only the executive summary is available.
